requirement:
Markdown reports only `Comment` attachments. Each HTML comment block whose
trimmed text starts with `<!--` and ends with `-->` is one attachment.
An inline HTML comment within a paragraph remains paragraph text, and
comment delimiters inside fenced code remain code.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.sdk.sources.markdown.attachments` has no implementation roots, and none are needed. Every clause states observable behavior of the Markdown source, not how it is built. - "Markdown reports only `Comment` attachments." This restricts the kind of attachment reported. A different implementation could use any parser or internal types and still report only comments, so the clause does not fix a type or signature. - "Each HTML comment block whose trimmed text starts with `` is one attachment." This is a classification rule on the output. A hand-written scanner, a Markdown AST walk or a regex would all give the same result, so no library or algorithm is prescribed. - "An inline HTML comment within a paragraph remains paragraph text." This describes what the output contains. How it is achieved is left open. - "Comment delimiters inside fenced code remain code." This is also observable behavior, and no delegation or interface is named. No clause names a required library, algorithm, signature, type, field, or delegation through a named interface. Tests can verify these behaviors, but no structural obligation needs `{impl}` evidence. behavioral: The `test.md` case in `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_languages_classify_only_their_attachment_syntax]` covers each obligation in `requirements.sdk.sources.markdown.attachments`. It asserts the exact `(kind, text)` list of attachments, so extra or missing attachments would fail. - **Each HTML comment block is one attachment.** The input has a single-line block `` and a multi-line block ``. The test expects exactly those two. Each is one attachment and keeps its full span, including the newline in the multi-line one. - **Only `Comment` attachments.** The assertion compares the kind, and every expected entry is `Comment`. The non-comment HTML block `
html
` produces nothing, so no other kind or non-comment block is reported. - **Trimmed text must start with ``.** The unterminated ` word.` yields no attachment. - **Delimiters in fenced code remain code.** The ```` ```html ```` fence containing `` yields no attachment. The obligations are all exercised and asserted. The `test.txt` and other-language cases are not needed for this requirement. The test carries a `{test}` marker for the subject.
